subject: Classical mechanics: projectile, incline with friction, energy with a spring, 1D collisions

items.method: Vertical motion alone: v_y0 = v0 sin(30 deg) = 10.0 m/s, v_y = 0 at the apex.

items.answer: Forces: weight mg (down), normal force N = m g cos(theta) perpendicular to the incline, kinetic friction f = mu_k N up along the incline. Along the incline (down positive): m a = m g sin(theta) - mu_k m g cos(theta).
items.method: Free-body diagram with axes along and perpendicular to the incline; no acceleration perpendicular so N = m g cos(theta).
The mass cancels in the equation of motion along the incline.

items.answer: The block stays at rest if mu_s m g cos(theta) >= m g sin(theta), i.e. mu_s >= tan 30 deg = 0.577
items.method: Static friction must balance the downhill component: mu_s >= tan(theta).

items.answer: v_A' = (m_A - m_B)/(m_A + m_B) x v_A = 1.0 m/s and v_B' = 2 m_A/(m_A + m_B) x v_A = 4.0 m/s, both in the original direction
items.method: Conservation of momentum and kinetic energy (or the elastic-collision formulas); check: 1 + 8 = 9 J.

items.answer: No external horizontal force acts on the carts (frictionless track), so total momentum is conserved in every collision. Kinetic energy is conserved only if no energy goes into deformation, heat or sound, which holds for the elastic case b) but not when the carts stick together.
items.method: Conceptual: internal forces conserve momentum; energy is conserved only for elastic collisions.
